thread.title: Qualcomm's Challenges May Only Get Worse - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM)

author: Mott Capital Management
title: Qualcomm's Challenges May Only Get Worse - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM)
text:
Shares of Qualcomm ( QCOM ) rallied on Dec. 10 after the company was able to block Apple ( AAPL ) from selling its older iPhone in China successfully. Apple is currently fighting this decision, and the company is still selling its phones. However, this is part of a much longer battle between the two technology giants. In 2017 Apple sued Qualcomm for $1 billion alleging the company is overcharging Apple for the rights to use Qualcomm's licensing. However, this is just one problem Qualcomm may be facing.
Should Qualcomm lose to Apple it could open the door to more lawsuits from other handset makers, and that could be very damaging to Qualcomm and its revenue stream. It's a significant risk that Qualcomm is rolling the dice on. The company already has had its revenue stream negatively impacted by the loss of Apple payments. Additionally, the company's revenue has been in a steady decline, and its recent stock buyback merely gives the appearance of growth.
Two Main Revenue Sources Qualcomm has two primary revenue streams: Qualcomm Technology Licensing ((QTL) and Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT). According to their latest 10-K , Qualcomm's QTL segment generated total revenue $5.2 billion, representing 23% of the company's total revenue in fiscal 2018. This revenue stream has dropped a staggering 33% since 2016 when it stood at $7.6 billion and represented 33% of the company's total revenue. The company noted in its 10-K that this revenue stream was negatively impacted by its dispute with Apple in 2018. The 10-K notes that QTL revenue was down $1.3 billion in 2018 vs. 2017.
Peak Revenue On a trailing-twelve-month basis, Qualcomm's revenue peaked in March 2015 at $27.50 billion and had since declined a stunning 17%. The litigation with Apple will only undoubtedly continue to weigh on Qualcomm's QTL business. Should other handset makers join in at some point down the road if Apple wins its case, then that revenue stream could fall even further. Analysts estimate revenue will climb to just $24.85 billion by the year 2021, still well below the previous highs.
QCOM Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts Where's The Growth? The company currently has very little growth on the table. It was the driving force behind the company's desperate attempt to buy NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ). According to Ycharts, analyst consensus revenue estimates for NXP in 2019 is $9.6 billion. It would have additionally made Qualcomm the leader in automotive chips. However, that deal fell through after the Chinese regulator body failed to approve the agreement, and Qualcomm was forced to pay NXP a $2 billion break-up fee.
Cash It left Qualcomm with loads of money, approximately $38 billion worth at the end of March 2018. Instead of looking to make another big acquisition or even a small addition to help correct its declining revenue stream the company decided to buy back $30 billion worth of stock. It's a move that allows earnings per shares to rise, giving the impression the company is growing, even though revenue is not. It also may suggest the company had no better use for the money. The declining revenue would suggest otherwise. It leaves the company with approximately $12 billion cash now.
No Growth The buyback may mask the company's troubles, but in reality, revenue is shrinking, and there's no growth to be seen. That's because the big stock buyback is merely reducing the share count, helping to boost earnings growth. But even worse Qualcomm saw its EPS fall to $3.69 in fiscal 2018 from $4.44 in 2016, a decline of 17%. According to Ycharts, consensus estimates show earnings aren't expected to eclipse those 2016 results until fiscal 2020.
QCOM Annual Actual EPS data by YCharts Risks Could Qualcomm ultimately prevail and defeat Apple? As the courts in China prove, anything is possible. If that should happen, then it could result in Qualcomm's QTL revenue stabilizing and potentially even starting once again to rise. The adoption of the fifth-generation of wireless technology, also known as 5G, could be a big benefit for Qualcomm as well, as handset makers and wireless providers start to roll out the new service. That may also be a big source of revenue for the company down the road.
For right now though there 's a lot of risk with Qualcomm's stock and perhaps the most glaring sign is that the company used all that cash to buy back its stock.
